solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Hard worker, say, follows architect (7)

indicatorNotes.follows: What follows comes second, so the worker goes after the architect.

blocks.note: Robert Adam, the 18th-century Scottish architect
a worker ant; 'say' flags an example

annotation.surface: A tough labourer taking orders from the architect on a building site.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hard worker' reads as one phrase, but 'Hard' alone is the definition and 'worker, say' is the insect.
annotation.definitionFit: Adamant once named a legendary unbreakable stone, so the word held literal hardness before it meant unyielding.

entries.clue: Pose with lettuce in buttonhole (6)

indicatorNotes.with: Together with 'in', it asks for the pose to have the lettuce inside it.
indicatorNotes.in: The lettuce goes in, inside the pose.

blocks.note: to pose is to put on an act
cos is a long-leaved lettuce, the romaine

annotation.surface: A dandy striking a pose with a lettuce leaf in his buttonhole instead of a flower.
annotation.walkthrough: The buttonhole is a verb: to buttonhole someone is to stop them and talk at them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym once 'buttonhole' is read as a verb: both mean stopping someone to talk to them.

entries.clue: A cola is unfortunately not a mixer (7)

indicatorNotes.unfortunately: Something that has gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters come out in the wrong order.

blocks.note: five of the letters to rearrange
the last two letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A barman's complaint that cola does not go well with spirits.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface mixer is a drink added to spirits; the definition's mixer is a sociable person.
annotation.definitionFit: A mixer in the social sense is someone who mingles easily; the answer describes a person who avoids company.

entries.clue: Answer cry involving chaps taking the same gender? (9)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a phrase describing the grammatical state; AGREEMENT is the noun for it.

indicatorNotes.involving: To involve is to wrap up, so the cry wraps around the chaps.

blocks.note: A is the standard abbreviation for answer
greet is Scots for to cry or weep
chaps are men

annotation.surface: A reply shouted about men who have decided to share one gender.
annotation.walkthrough: GREET for cry is Scottish usage, not a welcome. The definition is grammar: in languages like French an adjective takes the same gender as its noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example from grammar, where words matching in gender, number or case are said to agree.

entries.clue: Hike in electric vehicle parking (5)

blocks.note: trams run on electricity from overhead wires
P marks parking on road signs

annotation.surface: A rise in the charge for parking an electric car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hike' pretends to be a price rise; it is a long walk.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a long, tiring walk, noun or verb.

entries.clue: Higher offer terminated order (7)

blocks.note: when something has terminated it is over
to bid someone do something is to order them

annotation.surface: An auction where a higher offer ended the sale order.
annotation.walkthrough: BID for order is the old sense of command, as in 'do as you are bid', not an auction bid.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from auctions: an offer that goes above another, or above the thing's worth.

entries.clue: Abroad utterly without reservation (8)

blocks.note: abroad means out and about, away from home
right means completely, as in 'right royal' or 'right to the end'

annotation.surface: A traveller overseas who commits completely, holding nothing back.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition hides behind the travel word: 'without reservation' means unconditionally, not without a booking.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: done wholly and openly, with nothing held back.

entries.clue: Ireland rising under English is strangely frightening (5)

indicatorNotes.rising: In a down clue a word that rises reads from the bottom up, so it runs backwards.
indicatorNotes.under: In a down clue what is under something sits below it, so it comes second.

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

annotation.surface: A remark that an uprising in Ireland under English rule was strangely frightening.
annotation.walkthrough: The political uprising is only a reversal instruction; Ireland's name flips from EIRE to ERIE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: weird and unsettling, frightening in a way that is hard to name.

entries.clue: Litter on crossing in town (7)

indicatorNotes.on: In a down clue what is on top comes first, so the litter sits above the crossing.

blocks.note: litter is straw bedding for animals
a ford is a shallow river crossing

annotation.surface: Rubbish dropped on a pedestrian crossing in some town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Litter' is not rubbish but animal bedding.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the county town of Bedfordshire in the English Midlands.

entries.clue: Nations liaised about way of getting more drinking water (14)

annotation.definition: way of getting more drinking water

indicatorNotes.about: Letters moved about are shuffled into a new arrangement.

blocks.note: fourteen letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: Countries holding talks on how to provide more clean water.
annotation.walkthrough: A plausible news item about international water policy; the -ISATION ending is a good place to start the rearranging.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: removing salt from seawater turns it into water fit to drink.

entries.clue: Part of gardener’s path I considered rocky (7)

indicatorNotes.Part of: The answer is only part of the words that follow, sitting inside them.

blocks.note: gardener'S PATH I Considered

annotation.surface: A gardener thinking a stretch of the garden path looks stony.
annotation.walkthrough: A rare word, built from spar, a crystalline mineral; the hidden letters span three words.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose geological sense: the answer means like spar, a shiny crystalline mineral, so of rock.

entries.clue: What lengthens a possibly long wait on this in hospital? (9)

annotation.definition2: a possibly long wait on this in hospital?

blocks.note: a thing that pulls something out longer

blocks.clueFragment: a possibly long wait on this in hospital?
blocks.note: the carrying frame a patient lies on, perhaps for hours in a corridor

annotation.surface: A grumble about hospital waiting times dragging on.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is a gentle cryptic hint: patients are known to wait for hours on trolleys and stretchers.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: literally a thing that stretches, and the frame for carrying a patient.

entries.clue: Light resin (5)

blocks.note: the traffic light between red and green
tree resin that has fossilised into a golden gem

annotation.walkthrough: 'Light' is a traffic light, not a lamp or a lack of weight.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: the middle traffic signal takes its name from the colour of the fossil resin.

entries.clue: Eagles track, flying aloft on Chile air (5,10)

indicatorNotes.flying: Letters sent flying scatter and land in a new order.

blocks.note: fifteen letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: Eagles soaring on the air currents over Chile.
annotation.walkthrough: The Eagles are the American rock band, not birds, and a track is a song.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the 1977 title track of the Eagles' best-known album.

entries.clue: Historian in trouble penning year between lines (7)

indicatorNotes.penning: To pen something is to shut it in, so the trouble encloses the rest.
indicatorNotes.between: The year sits between the two lines.

blocks.note: care is worry or trouble
L for line; the first of the two lines
Y is the abbreviation for year
the second line

annotation.surface: A historian in difficulty after writing a year's events between the lines.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lines' gives two Ls, one each side of Y, and that group goes inside the trouble.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Thomas Carlyle wrote the famous history of the French Revolution.

entries.clue: I’m performing with orchestra? Could be (11)

annotation.definition: I’m performing with orchestra? Could be

indicatorNotes.performing: Letters performing are put through their paces, rearranged.

blocks.note: two of the letters to rearrange
the other nine letters

annotation.surface: Someone announcing they are performing with an orchestra, and wondering who they might be.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: 'Could be' invites you to guess who might be speaking.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue is a line a choir's director might well say before a concert with orchestra.

entries.clue: Supplier of current device? (11)

blocks.note: a wholesaler who passes goods on to shops
the petrol-engine part that sends current to each spark plug in turn

annotation.surface: A question about who supplies electricity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supplier of current' reads as an electricity company, but the split falls after 'Supplier'.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of handing things out, goods to shops or current to spark plugs.

entries.clue: Prickly part of southern tree (5)

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a pine is a tree

annotation.surface: A southern tree with a thorny bit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prickly part of' looks like it wants a part of a tree; it is the definition, and 'of' only links.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a sharp prickle, as on a cactus or hedgehog.

entries.clue: Maybe thirty-one or over in game (7)

indicatorNotes.over: Turned over, the word is flipped to run backwards.

blocks.note: 31 is a prime number; 'maybe' flags an example
the word itself

annotation.surface: A card game where the score is perhaps thirty-one or more.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Thirty-one or over' sounds like a score in a card game; 31 is just a prime number and 'over' flips OR.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an old Tudor card game, an ancestor of poker.

entries.clue: Last-minute recovery by one side? (9)

blocks.note: last-minute means late
a rally is a recovery, as by a team or a market

annotation.surface: A team pulling back from defeat at the last minute.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as sport, with 'one side' a team; it is the definition, meaning sideways.
annotation.definitionFit: The adverb means to or from the side, which the question mark flags as a stretch of 'by one side'.

entries.clue: Perhaps be prone as a carpenter to accept results of one’s own deeds (3,2,3,3,3,3,4)

annotation.answer: LIE IN THE BED ONE HAS MADE
annotation.definition: accept results of one’s own deeds
annotation.definition2: Perhaps be prone as a carpenter

blocks.clueFragment: Perhaps be prone as a carpenter
blocks.note: a carpenter who built a piece of bedroom furniture, lying flat on it

blocks.clueFragment: accept results of one’s own deeds
blocks.note: the everyday idiom, from the proverb about making your bed

annotation.surface: A carpenter lying down, then accepting the consequences of what he has done.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic hint reading the proverb literally: a carpenter has really made the bed and lies prone in it.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to put up with the unpleasant results of one's own choices.

entries.clue: Book vault bare after November (7)

indicatorNotes.bare: A word stripped bare loses its outer covering, its first and last letters.
indicatorNotes.after: What comes after is placed second, behind the November.

blocks.note: the first three letters of November, shortened as on a calendar
a cellar is a vault, and bared of its first and last letters it leaves the inner four

annotation.surface: Someone leaping over a book in a bare room after November.
annotation.walkthrough: The vault is an underground room, a cellar, not a leap.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a short novel is one kind of book.

entries.clue: Last of lime preserve put into bitter drink as source of sweetness? (9)

indicatorNotes.Last of: Only the last letter of 'lime' is used.
indicatorNotes.put into: The pieces are put into the drink, which surrounds them.

blocks.note: bitter is a kind of British ale
the last letter of lime
to keep something is to preserve it

annotation.surface: A recipe putting lime and preserves into a bitter drink to sweeten it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bitter drink' is one thing, beer, which wraps round the rest. The question mark signals a playful definition: honey is the sweetness.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the person who keeps hives supplies honey, hence sweetness.

entries.clue: Demonstrate round residence topless come what may (7)

indicatorNotes.round: The first word goes round the second, enclosing it.
indicatorNotes.topless: In a down clue the top is the first letter, so it goes.

blocks.note: to show is to demonstrate
HOME without its top letter

annotation.surface: A protest outside a house by topless demonstrators, whatever happens.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface demonstrators are protesters; 'topless' just removes the first letter of the residence.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom match: both mean by some means or other, whatever it takes.

entries.clue: Central America region containing a waterfall (8)

indicatorNotes.containing: The region holds the A inside it.

blocks.note: CA is the abbreviation for Central America
a tract is an area of land, a region
the word itself

annotation.surface: A region of Central America with a waterfall in it.
annotation.walkthrough: A geography-book surface; the A drops in after the first letter of the region.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a large, steep fall of water; the eye condition takes its name from it.

entries.clue: E-number — note it in a drop (8)

indicatorNotes.in: The note and 'it' go in, inside the drop.

blocks.note: the word itself
a dive is a sudden drop, as in prices
D is a musical note
the word itself

annotation.surface: A food label about an E-number, noting it appears in a drop.
annotation.walkthrough: E-numbers are the codes used in Europe to label approved food ingredients, which is why a food label is the picture.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: each E-number codes one approved food additive.

entries.clue: Sadly duke is giving the job to Liberal unknown (15)

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
the word itself
to appoint someone is to give them the job
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

annotation.surface: A regretful note that a duke is handing a post to an unknown Liberal politician.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' looks like a comment on the appointment but is the definition itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as sentence adverbs: both express regret that things turned out badly.

entries.clue: Male, the antithesis of earth god (6)

indicatorNotes.the antithesis of: An antithesis is a direct opposite, so the word is turned the opposite way round.

blocks.note: a male is a he
earth is soil

annotation.surface: A male sky god described as the opposite of an earth god.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Earth god' looks like one phrase, but 'god' alone is the definition and the opposite of the earth is just the word backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Greek god of the sun.

entries.clue: Ignoring bishop, big number managed church in innocence (9)

indicatorNotes.Ignoring: The bishop, B, is ignored and left out of 'big'.

blocks.note: BIG without B, the chess abbreviation for bishop
No. is the abbreviation for number
to run a business is to manage it
CE is the Church of England

annotation.surface: A tale of a church run by a large congregation that shut its bishop out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Big number' reads as one phrase but splits: BIG loses the bishop and number is NO.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of not knowing: innocence of the facts is lack of knowledge of them.

entries.clue: Stays with body (7)

blocks.note: a verb: stays put, is left behind
a corpse, what is left of a person

annotation.surface: Someone who sticks with a group.
annotation.walkthrough: The body is a corpse, not an organisation one stays with.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: a verb for staying and a noun for what is left of the dead.

entries.clue: Forbidding being home when relative is coming round (8)

indicatorNotes.is coming round: The relative comes round the home, enclosing it.

blocks.note: a sister is a relative
being at home is being in

annotation.surface: A gloomy feeling of being home when a relation visits.
annotation.walkthrough: A sly surface about dreading family visits, where 'coming round' means visiting.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe a threatening, ominous look.

entries.clue: Aren’t involved in interaction between heavenly bodies (14)

indicatorNotes.involved: Letters that are involved are tangled together, rearranged.
indicatorNotes.in: The jumbled letters go in, inside the interaction.

blocks.note: interplay is interaction
the letters of AREN'T rearranged

annotation.surface: A denial that anyone is involved in the relationship between planets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Aren't involved' reads as a denial, but 'involved' is the anagram signal and 'in' the insertion.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: between the planets, which are heavenly bodies.

entries.clue: Something useful like gel (5)

blocks.note: as means like
a jelly gels when it sets

annotation.surface: Hair gel praised as handy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gel' is a verb here, to firm up.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a useful or valuable thing or quality.

entries.clue: Rent to get outside old city (7)

indicatorNotes.get outside: The rent gets outside the old, wrapping round it.

blocks.note: rent is the old past participle of rend, to tear
O is the abbreviation for old
the word itself

annotation.surface: A tenant paying rent to move out of an old city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rent' is not a payment but torn, as in 'a garment rent in two'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Canada's largest city.

entries.clue: Part of lighthouse is large — money put up by Royal Navy (7)

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large
in poker the ante is the stake put up before the deal
RN is the Royal Navy

annotation.surface: A lighthouse built with a lot of money from the Royal Navy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Money put up' sounds like funding; it is a gambling stake.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialist sense: the glazed room at the top of a lighthouse that houses the light.

entries.clue: Light feel to feathers (5,4)

blocks.note: to feel is to touch
down is soft fine feathers

annotation.surface: Feathers that are soft and light to the touch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Light' is a verb, to land, as a bird lights on a branch.
annotation.definitionFit: A less familiar verb sense: to light is to come down and settle, as a plane or bird does.

entries.clue: Raises pastry like a confident newcomer (7)

blocks.note: to up a price is to raise it
a tart is a pastry

annotation.surface: A new baker whose pastry rises well.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer works as an adjective, as in 'an upstart rival', so it fits 'like a confident newcomer'.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjectival use: newly risen and presumptuously sure of oneself.

entries.clue: A box with insipid sweetener (9)

blocks.note: the word itself
to spar is to box
tame means dull, insipid

annotation.surface: A box of bland artificial sweetener.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Box' is the verb, to fight, not a container.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the artificial sweetener used in many diet drinks.

entries.clue: Room mostly small and in bad condition (7)

indicatorNotes.mostly: Mostly means most but not all, so the last letter goes.

blocks.note: PARLOUR without its last letter
S is the abbreviation for small

annotation.surface: An estate agent admitting a room is mostly small and run down.
annotation.walkthrough: A parlour is an old-fashioned sitting room.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an old contraction of perilous, describing a dangerous or dire state.

entries.clue: More than one current royal castle dismissing soldiers (5)

indicatorNotes.dismissing: The soldiers are dismissed, sent out of the word.

blocks.note: Windsor Castle, a residence of the British monarch
OR, other ranks, the ordinary soldiers, are removed

annotation.surface: The current royals at Windsor sending the guards away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current royal' reads as the reigning family, but the definition is 'More than one current', air currents.
annotation.definitionFit: A plural by description: moving air currents, several of them.

entries.clue: Beat decisively after ordering recount (7)

indicatorNotes.ordering: Ordering puts the letters into a new order.

blocks.note: seven letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: An election won by a landslide after a recount was ordered.
annotation.walkthrough: The election picture is apt: a recount that confirms a crushing win.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to defeat heavily.

entries.clue: Sweetbrier, for instance, with insect in occupation (9)

indicatorNotes.in: The insect goes in, inside the occupation.

blocks.note: e.g., for example
one's line is one's trade or occupation
an ant is an insect

annotation.surface: A sweetbrier plant infested with insects.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweetbrier, for instance' looks like a definition by example, but 'for instance' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: two names for the same wild rose.

entries.clue: Write tons about a king’s father? (6)

indicatorNotes.about: The writing and tons go about the A and king, surrounding them.

blocks.note: to pen is to write
the word itself
R is Rex, king
T is the abbreviation for tons

annotation.surface: A biographer writing reams about a king's father.
annotation.walkthrough: 'King's father' is a trap: the 's is 'is', linking the wordplay to 'father?'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: a father is one kind.

entries.clue: Vehicle quickly does for tortoiseshell (8)

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
apace means quickly

annotation.surface: A speeding car running over a tortoiseshell cat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Does for' reads as kills; it only links, saying the wordplay serves for the definition. The tortoiseshell here is the shell itself, not a cat.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialist term: the hard upper shell of a tortoise or crab.

entries.clue: Strangely inane passage in American film (5,4)

indicatorNotes.Strangely: Letters arranged strangely are in an odd order.

blocks.note: INANE rearranged
a hall is a passage or corridor

annotation.surface: A critic's complaint about a silly scene in an American film.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Passage' tempts as a scene in the film; it is a corridor.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Woody Allen's 1977 comedy.

entries.clue: Department head is blocking one who makes the money (8)

indicatorNotes.blocking: What blocks something sits in its way, inside it.

blocks.note: a minter strikes coins at a mint
the word itself

annotation.surface: A government department head obstructing whoever controls the money.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a politician blocking the Treasury; 'one who makes the money' is literal, a coin maker.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description of the British cabinet role that heads a government department.

entries.clue: Superconducting cable that’s easy to take (4,2,5,10)

annotation.definition: Superconducting cable that’s easy to take

blocks.note: a superconductor has zero electrical resistance, so the cable is literally the one that resists least
the everyday sense: the easiest course of action

annotation.surface: An engineer describing a new cable that is simple to lay.
annotation.walkthrough: The physics is a cryptic hint; the real meaning is the idiom for the easiest option.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the course that is easiest to follow, read literally as a wire with no resistance.

entries.clue: Enthusiastic players regularly more than half musical (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: Taking letters at regular intervals: every other one.
indicatorNotes.more than half: Only more than half of the word is kept, its last four of seven letters.

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of pLaYeRs
the last four letters of musICAL

annotation.surface: Keen performers who mostly play in musicals.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the idiom 'wax lyrical', to talk with gushing enthusiasm.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiomatic sense: effusive, as in waxing lyrical about something.

entries.clue: Representation banned including Local Education Authority (7)

indicatorNotes.including: The ban includes the authority, holding it inside.

blocks.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, forbidden
an LEA ran state schools in an English area

annotation.surface: A depiction banned by the local education authority.
annotation.walkthrough: The less common spelling of taboo is needed for the letters to work.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a picture or staged scene represents something.

entries.clue: Leg and shin injured in course run at school (7)

indicatorNotes.injured: Something injured is damaged out of shape, its letters rearranged.

blocks.note: seven letters to rearrange; 'and' only joins them

annotation.surface: A pupil hurting leg and shin on the school cross-country course.
annotation.walkthrough: The course is a school subject, not a running track.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of the subjects taught as a course at school.

entries.clue: One who laments more piercing (6)

blocks.note: a mourner who wails over the dead, in the Irish tradition
sharper, as a blade or wind

annotation.surface: A mourner whose cries are especially shrill.
annotation.walkthrough: Keening is the Irish tradition of wailing over the dead.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: a noun for a wailing mourner and a comparative for sharper.

entries.clue: Sun’s final radiance ruined by this? (4,5)

annotation.definition: Sun’s final radiance ruined by this?

indicatorNotes.ruined: What is ruined is broken up, the letters rearranged.

blocks.note: the last letter of sun
the other eight letters

annotation.surface: Sunshine spoilt by some ritual.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: a ritual that worked would end the sunshine.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes a ritual meant to bring rain, which would spoil the sun's radiance.

entries.clue: Thoroughly clean off the mark after party (2,3)

indicatorNotes.after: In a down clue what comes after goes below, second.

blocks.note: a do is a party
a guess that is out is inaccurate, off the mark

annotation.surface: Scrubbing away a stain after a party.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrasal verb is British: to give a room a thorough clean or tidy.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom for cleaning or clearing out a room thoroughly.

entries.clue: Formerly linking wager with error in it (7)

blocks.note: a bet is a wager
W is the abbreviation for with
the word itself
a cross marks an error

annotation.surface: A bet that once went wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' is not a link: it is W. 'Formerly' flags an archaic word.
annotation.definitionFit: An archaic form of between, the preposition that links two things.

entries.clue: A learner excluded from Icelandic parliament matter (5)

indicatorNotes.excluded from: The A and learner are shut out of the parliament's name.

blocks.note: the Althing, Iceland's parliament
A plus L, the learner driver's plate, removed

annotation.surface: A trainee barred from Iceland's parliament over some issue.
annotation.walkthrough: The Althing is one of the world's oldest parliaments.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an affair or business, as in 'a matter of taste'.

entries.clue: Tugs plying around a river (5)

indicatorNotes.plying: Tugs that ply move to and fro, and so do the letters.
indicatorNotes.around: The tugs gather around the A as they rearrange.

blocks.note: four letters to rearrange
the fifth letter

annotation.surface: Tugboats working a river.
annotation.walkthrough: The picture is exactly right: tugs plying on the river.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the longest river of the Iberian Peninsula, reaching the sea at Lisbon.

entries.clue: Below par score European composer nearly sent back (5)

indicatorNotes.nearly: Nearly means not quite all, so the last letter goes.
indicatorNotes.sent back: Sent back, the word is reversed.

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
Edward Elgar, the English composer, missing his last letter

annotation.surface: A European composer getting a poor mark and being sent home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Below par' sounds like a poor showing, but in golf below par is good.
annotation.definitionFit: A golf term: two strokes under par on a hole.

entries.clue: Nickname is too menacing somehow (11)

indicatorNotes.somehow: Somehow means in some way or other, so the letters take some new order.

blocks.note: eleven letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A nickname that sounds rather too threatening.
annotation.walkthrough: A rare verb from Latin cognomen, a surname or nickname.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to give someone a byname.

entries.clue: Mixing of sheep among allotment hedges (11)

indicatorNotes.hedges: To hedge is to surround, as a hedge surrounds a field.

blocks.note: among means in
a teg is a sheep in its second year
a ration is an allotted share

annotation.surface: Sheep getting mixed in among the hedges of an allotment.
annotation.walkthrough: An allotment here is a share, not a rented vegetable plot, and its hedges are the verb that wraps the sheep.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the social sense: bringing groups together into one whole.

entries.clue: Even now cutting delayed child’s clothing (7)

indicatorNotes.cutting: What cuts something goes into it, splitting it.

blocks.note: delayed means late
yet means even now, still

annotation.surface: A late delivery of a baby's clothes, still to be cut out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delayed child' looks like one phrase; 'delayed' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialist word: the full set of clothes prepared for a newborn baby.

entries.clue: Like a little brother you get annoyed when ace is lost (7)

indicatorNotes.when ace is lost: The ace, A, is lost from the word.

blocks.note: the word itself
